title: EPAM Concurrency and Performance
description: Async Python, event loop, asyncio, threading, locks, race conditions, multiprocessing, profiling, caching, Redis basics, and N+1 queries.

questions.prompt: What kind of workload benefits most from async/await?
questions.explanation: Async lets one event loop switch tasks while operations wait on I/O.

concept_panel.title: Async/Await
concept_panel.explanation: Async lets one event loop switch tasks while operations wait on I/O.
concept_panel.practical_example: Await several integration API calls without blocking the server.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand async Python's actual benefit.

questions.prompt: What does the event loop coordinate?
questions.explanation: The event loop runs coroutines and resumes them when awaited I/O is ready.

concept_panel.title: Event Loop
concept_panel.explanation: The event loop runs coroutines and resumes them when awaited I/O is ready.
concept_panel.practical_example: asyncio gathers multiple HTTP calls and resumes each when a response arrives.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand async runtime behavior.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with CPU-heavy work inside an async endpoint?
questions.explanation: CPU-heavy work does not yield control, so it can block other coroutines.

concept_panel.title: Blocking in Async
concept_panel.explanation: CPU-heavy work does not yield control, so it can block other coroutines.
concept_panel.practical_example: Move heavy forecasting to a worker process.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you avoid event-loop blocking.

questions.prompt: When can threads help in Python?
questions.explanation: Threads can overlap blocking I/O, but shared state requires care.

concept_panel.title: Threading
concept_panel.explanation: Threads can overlap blocking I/O, but shared state requires care.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use threads for blocking SDK calls if async APIs are unavailable.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know realistic thread use cases.

questions.explanation: Locks prevent multiple threads from modifying shared state at the same time.

concept_panel.title: Locks
concept_panel.explanation: Locks prevent multiple threads from modifying shared state at the same time.
concept_panel.practical_example: Guard an in-memory counter updated by many worker threads.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand synchronization.

options: A bug where timing changes the outcome
questions.answer: A bug where timing changes the outcome
questions.explanation: Race conditions happen when concurrent operations interleave unpredictably around shared state.

concept_panel.title: Race Conditions
concept_panel.explanation: Race conditions happen when concurrent operations interleave unpredictably around shared state.
concept_panel.practical_example: Two threads increment the same counter and one update is lost.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can reason about concurrent correctness.

options: CPU-bound work that can run in separate processes
questions.answer: CPU-bound work that can run in separate processes
questions.explanation: Multiprocessing can use multiple CPU cores because work runs in separate processes.

concept_panel.title: Multiprocessing
concept_panel.explanation: Multiprocessing can use multiple CPU cores because work runs in separate processes.
concept_panel.practical_example: Run feature engineering or model scoring in worker processes.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you choose the right execution model.

options: async for I/O, multiprocessing for CPU
questions.answer: async for I/O, multiprocessing for CPU
questions.explanation: Choose the model based on the bottleneck: waiting on I/O, shared-state coordination, or CPU work.

concept_panel.title: When to Use What
concept_panel.explanation: Choose the model based on the bottleneck: waiting on I/O, shared-state coordination, or CPU work.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use async for API calls and processes for heavy forecasting jobs.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you match tools to bottlenecks.

options: Profile to find the real bottleneck
questions.answer: Profile to find the real bottleneck
questions.explanation: Profiling prevents guessing. It shows where time is actually spent.

concept_panel.title: Profiling
concept_panel.explanation: Profiling prevents guessing. It shows where time is actually spent.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use profiling to discover that serialization, not SQL, dominates response time.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you optimize from evidence.

options: Repeated expensive reads that tolerate staleness
questions.answer: Repeated expensive reads that tolerate staleness
questions.explanation: Caches reduce repeated work but introduce invalidation and staleness decisions.

concept_panel.title: Caching
concept_panel.explanation: Caches reduce repeated work but introduce invalidation and staleness decisions.
concept_panel.practical_example: Cache dashboard metadata that changes rarely.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you know caching trade-offs.

questions.prompt: What is Redis commonly used for?
options: Fast cache, session, queue, or rate-limit state
questions.answer: Fast cache, session, queue, or rate-limit state
questions.explanation: Redis is an in-memory data store often used for fast operational state.

concept_panel.title: Redis Basics
concept_panel.explanation: Redis is an in-memory data store often used for fast operational state.
concept_panel.practical_example: Store a short-lived dashboard cache key in Redis.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you understand common infrastructure components.

questions.prompt: A page loads 100 rows then queries details row by row. What is likely happening?
questions.explanation: N+1 query patterns create one parent query plus one child query per row. Use eager loading or bulk queries.

concept_panel.title: N+1 Queries
concept_panel.explanation: N+1 query patterns create one parent query plus one child query per row. Use eager loading or bulk queries.
concept_panel.practical_example: Use selectinload to fetch related orders for all users.
concept_panel.interview_insight: Interviewers usually ask this concept to evaluate whether you can detect ORM performance problems.

coding_challenges.title: EPAM Concurrency and Performance status classifier
coding_challenges.instructions: Implement classify_status_code(code: int) -> str. Return success for 200-299, redirect for 300-399, client_error for 400-499, server_error for 500-599, and unknown otherwise.
coding_challenges.explanation: The challenge reinforces deterministic branching, status-code categories, and local test execution.
